DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) with secondary urinary tract symptoms.

The combination of chronic frequency, nocturia, weak stream, incomplete emptying, and negative infectious workup strongly points to prostate enlargement obstructing the urethra. The elevated PSA and CT findings likely support this mechanical obstruction, possibly with small stones or calcifications.
